column2: The civilian government will control appointments. Trust in the army will grow, although coordinating plans will take longer.
General Staff Doctrine
The general staff will receive broad powers over planning and unit organisation. The cabinet will have to share political initiative with it.
Reach the Sea
We have no port of our own. Headquarters is preparing a plan for Fada and Hoskheit, but that will not produce ships.
Coastal Defence
We will establish a coastal command and begin training specialists to protect ports and coastal routes.
Bring the Ports under Oversight
The port service will organise cargo inspections and depot protection. Smuggling channels must no longer offer foreign agents an open door.
Protect the Sea Lanes
Research into coastal craft and escorts. Battleships are not part of the programme.
Affordable Shipbuilding
We will expand ship-repair facilities in one of our controlled ports. Two dockyards will provide the foundation for a permanent naval programme.
Escort Duty
We will train crews to escort transports and coordinate naval operations with shore services.
Deny the Enemy Fleet
We will fortify the coastline and strengthen the ports' anti-air defences. The enemy will have to fight for a landing before it reaches the mountain roads.
Inspect the Clients
A dependency spirit binds the client's port. Inspections increase resistance, but do not replace the leader.
Their Port Is Not Ours
A permanent base in an ally's territory requires its consent. Violating that rule breaks the coalition.
Coastal Shipping under Staff Direction
Military escorts take priority over merchant routes. This does not unlock general-staff focuses for Barchel.
Aircrew Cadres
We will train pilots, mechanics and controllers. New research will allow us to choose an aircraft the country can maintain on its own.
Airfields
We will prepare an airfield for two new air groups and conduct staff exercises. Construction will take place in a controlled region where the base can still be expanded.
Shield the Skies
We will strengthen ground-based air defence and accelerate fighter development to protect our cities and mountain passes.
Support the Troops
We will coordinate aviation with ground units. New aircraft must help the army where mountain roads cannot carry heavy artillery.
Reconnaissance over the Passes
Fifteen intelligence points on both neighbours and a decision to repeat the sortie.
Orders for Private Aircraft Suppliers

We will unlock a repeatable purchase of one hundred basic fighters for 120 treasury units. The focus itself prepares the procurement arrangements; money is deducted only when the decision is selected.
Domestic Assembly
We will expand military production and prepare our own aviation programme. A new factory and two research bonuses will reduce dependence on foreign supplies.
Air Power as Pressure
A strike against a hub as an ultimatum. This is not liberation.
Do Not Strike an Ally
Strikes on a partner's hubs are forbidden. The coalition rests on this rule.
Reconnaissance before Gestures
The directorate strengthens reconnaissance rather than staging a demonstrative raid.
The Founder's Cabinet

Victory gave the country a name, but its departments are still empty. We will appoint the people who ran the districts, depots and safe houses during the war. The alliance will receive a permanent name, and the ministries will cease to be vacant posts.
The Founder's Politics
Victory brought together people with different visions of the future. Shabrat must decide whether to become the arbiter of a strong centre or the guarantor of independent civilian institutions.
Steland Hegemony
We will concentrate political initiative in the government. Some supporters of district autonomy will withdraw, but the cabinet will be able to prepare a common course more quickly.
Freedom against Slavery
We will recognise the district councils' and assembly's right to influence decisions. Coordination will take time, but the new government will gain broader support.
An Archive, Not a Sentence upon the Country

We will open the archives to researchers and the commission investigating the old regime's crimes. Working with these documents must become a permanent service, not an extension of personal vengeance.
Unity of the Victors
The council under Shabrat loses its veto over appointments. This decree does not revoke the guarantees to the SRP.
Emergency Powers
We will grant industry emergency powers for 180 days. Military output and war support will rise, along with administrative expenditure.
Subordinate the Centres of Power
District commissioners will answer to the government. A single chain of decisions will reduce administrative costs and expand recruitment capacity.
Limit Political Competition
We will concentrate political activity within registered organisations. This will strengthen the government's initiative, but narrow the scope for independent research.
The Course Is Set
We will commit to a strong centre and regional primacy. Shabrat will remain in charge, and the civilian republican path will close.
The Founder's Name in Law
We will make the founder the final authority in disputes between departments and districts. His standing will accelerate the work of the political apparatus.
A Regional System
We will prepare industry for permanent external commitments. Greater utilisation of military factories will require a more expensive administrative apparatus.
The Reckoning with Kefreyt
We will review the terms of Kefreyt's contracts and prepare the government's position for negotiations over a new border settlement.
Political Guarantees from Kefreyt
We will ask Kefreyt to recognise Steland's political primacy. It may accept or refuse. Refusal leaves military preparations available; war will not begin without a separate order.
Plan the Mountain Campaign

Following Kefreyt's refusal, headquarters will draw up a campaign plan. First, we must fund 35 days of supply preparation, then decide within 90 days whether to launch the offensive. Kefreyt will receive a warning and time to prepare its defence.
Challenge the Northern Mandate
We will ask Nodrul to recognise a reversal of the relationship: henceforth, decisions in the region will require Steland's consent. Refusal does not start a war automatically.
Plan the Northern Campaign

Following Nodrul's refusal, we will prepare supplies and reconnaissance for the northern front. A separate programme will take 35 days and require funding. The order to go to war will remain the government's decision.
Dependent Governments
We will bring neighbours that recognise our primacy into a regional league. Only governments which have already accepted the relevant terms will join.
The Price of Primacy
We will establish a permanent apparatus to coordinate external forces. The army will gain better organisation at the cost of additional administrative expenditure.
Assembly of the Districts
Laws will pass through the assembly. Shabrat remains head of state, but loses some of his day-to-day influence.
Independent Institutions
We will establish an independent judiciary and a permanent representative chamber. Predictable rules will lower administrative expenditure and support research.
The Army Answers to Civilians
The government will receive the right to approve military commanders. If Sotnikov is available, his experience will be retained in a civilian defence council.
The Charter Is Established
We will secure civilian rule and the independence of representative institutions. Shabrat remains head of state, but the hegemonic path closes.
Political Competition
We will open political competition within the new order. Gornin and Tikh will be able to present their programmes before a possible transfer of power.
Power That Can Be Passed On
Shabrat will choose between continuing to lead and transferring power to one of the nominated civilian successors.
Emergencies Have an Expiry Date
We will define the limits of emergency mobilisation. During war, a temporary reserve call-up may be declared separately at a cost in command power.
Political Preparation in the Neighbouring States
We will establish a permanent service to monitor our neighbours. For a separate payment, it will be able to update intelligence on their armed forces.
Talk to Those beyond the Border
We will establish links with civilian groups and specialists in neighbouring countries. Economic intelligence will help the government assess the consequences of intervention.
The Intervention Crisis
A stronger border service and a reserve of command power will allow us to face an open crisis prepared. This step does not yet declare war.
War of Liberation

Open border crises will be settled by war with the neighbour concerned. If crises with Kefreyt and Nodrul are active at the same time, we will have to fight on two fronts. A war already under way will receive the same plan for a post-war settlement.
Transitional Administration
We will fund a temporary administration and offer defeated neighbours a transitional agreement. The political outcome depends on their response.
An Independent Government
The transitional commissions are concluding their work. Instead of permanently supervising our neighbours, the cabinet will concentrate on civilian construction and reduce administrative expenditure.
A Coalition of Equals
We will bring governments that accepted the terms of liberation into a defensive coalition. Every participant must confirm its choice.
The Chain of Command
Without the political founder, headquarters assumes responsibility for coordinating scattered units. A unified chain of orders will restore control.
Field Commanders
Sotnikov will use the experience of field commanders to accelerate operational preparation.
District Formations
The districts provide men to headquarters, not to the council.
The Staff State
The administration answers to the chain of command, not the assembly.
Two Threats, One Headquarters
Intelligence will assess Nodrul's and Kefreyt's forces. A change of commander does not erase the information or the common task of defence.
The Limits of Military Rule
